**Group:** Dinoflagellates  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

A small athecate (naked) dinoflagellate, usually elongate to top- or spindle-shaped, characteristically with a small epicone (the part above the girdle) sitting over a larger hypocone, and a displaced cingulum. No cellulose thecal plates are visible, and several species are heterotrophic. Key features: small naked cell, small epicone over a larger hypocone, displaced girdle.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **gyrodinium** | Gyrodinium has a strongly displaced sigmoid girdle with epicone and hypocone of more similar size; Katodinium characteristically has a small epicone over a larger hypocone. |
| **akashiwo** | Akashiwo is a large, dorsoventrally flattened naked dinoflagellate; Katodinium is small and elongate with an asymmetric epicone and hypocone. |
